Bash allow rules can be bypassed with a heredoc

With an allow rule such as `Bash(git status:*)`, Tropos auto-approves a command when every simple command in it matches an allowed prefix. Heredoc bodies are raw text, but the command splitter treats quotes inside them as real shell quotes. So this command:

git status <<X
'
X
rm -rf y
'

is seen as a single `git status ...` command (the `'` in the heredoc body opens a "quote" that swallows the following lines) and gets auto-approved, even though the shell runs `rm -rf y` as a separate command.

Expected: commands that use a heredoc (`cat <<EOF ...`, `cat <<-EOF ...`) or a herestring (`cat <<<hello`) should be flagged as unsafe by `splitBashCommand` in src/permissions/rules.ts, so they never silently match an allow rule. Plain input redirection such as `bun test < input.txt` must stay safe, and a quoted `<<` (`echo "<<"`, `echo '<<'`) is just text and must stay safe too.

Add or update tests as appropriate.
